title: Release changelog extraction treats version headings inside fenced examples as release boundaries
body:
Found at `0ece2cf2c2745c3574ffb65dbabdfcadd7163c14`, `scripts/create-github-release.rs:108-143`, while auditing https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/55. The section scanner treats Markdown headings inside fenced example code as real release boundaries, silently deleting the rest of the notes.

Minimal CHANGELOG.md:

````markdown
## [1.2.3]

Example:

```md
## [9.9.9]
```

Remaining details.

## [1.2.2]
old
````

Expected: the 1.2.3 body contains the whole fenced example and `Remaining details.`. Actual: the body ends at `Example:` and the opening fence, leaving invalid Markdown and dropping real release information. A requested version that appears only inside a fenced example can also select example text as release notes.

Reproduce from the template root (no real publishing):

```sh
# In an isolated copy of the template, put the example below in CHANGELOG.md.
# Stub gh so this rehearsal cannot publish:
fixture=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$fixture"' EXIT
printf '#!/bin/sh\ncat\n' > "$fixture/gh"
chmod +x "$fixture/gh"
PATH="$fixture:$PATH" CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 rust-script scripts/create-github-release.rs --release-version 1.2.3 --repository fixture/repo
```

The JS and Python snapshot functions were executed offline and both returned the truncated body. The Rust source has the same boundary error in `next_section_re`, which matches `^## [` without fence state; the above CLI reproduction uses a local gh stub. No Rust template build was run on the constrained downstream machine.

Workaround: use indented example code or avoid version-shaped headings inside fenced changelog examples until the scanner is fixed. Do not silently delete the example or the later prose from the actual release.

Suggested fix: find exact release headings only outside Markdown code fences (both backticks and tildes, matching closing delimiter/length), or parse Markdown to an AST and slice by top-level heading offsets. Preserve body bytes/indentation, fail explicitly on missing required entries, and add tests for a fenced next-version heading, a target version only inside a fence, CRLF and multiple change subsections. The downstream PR adds these regressions in `js/tests/ci-github-release.test.js` and fixes its shared release-content helper; the Rust/Python publication programs are template-specific and are not vendored into the product.

title: Security workflow can pass while CodeQL reports unresolved findings
body:
At snapshot 0ece2cf2c2745c3574ffb65dbabdfcadd7163c14, .github/workflows/security.yml runs github/codeql-action/analyze and its terminal gate observes only job outcomes. Analyze succeeds when analysis and upload succeed, even when SARIF contains findings. This is the same integration gap tracked in the JavaScript template #266 and Python template #122; it is not evidence of a vulnerability in this Rust template itself.

Reproducible downstream evidence: https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/actions/runs/40790641642 succeeded at dc30f00aefb2c1a89c64bf7e7fa78ef80a860fe7 while its JavaScript SARIF contained 50 findings. https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/53 archives that SARIF; replaying it with `node js/scripts/check-codeql-results.mjs PATH_TO_REPORT_DIRECTORY` exits nonzero and reports 50 findings. A synthetic regression is one valid SARIF 2.1.0 CodeQL run containing one result: analyze/upload success must not imply a clean security gate.

Workaround: explicitly require the separate Code Scanning check in branch rules rather than relying only on the aggregate workflow.

Suggested fix: give analyze an explicit `output` directory; afterward run a dependency-free SARIF gate that rejects absent/malformed reports, unsuccessful invocations and unresolved findings in every file/run, including warning/note severities. Keep all queries and the normal upload. Preserve the SARIF artifact even after gate failure. For reviewed intentional APIs, scope any exception to rule, file, line and full source-file SHA256 with a reason and test reference rather than disabling a query.

Reusable implementation and regression tests: https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-52-966c0184cc29/js/scripts/check-codeql-results.mjs and https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-52-966c0184cc29/js/tests/ci-codeql-results.test.js. Tests cover missing/invalid reports, multiple files/runs, every severity, execution failure, changed exception digests and CLI exit status.

Official analyze input/output contract: https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/main/analyze/action.yml.

title: Missing lychee report is reported as all_archived=true and exit 0
body:
Found during the complete template comparison for https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/44 (issue 43).

## Reproduction

At revision `0ece2cf2c2745c3574ffb65dbabdfcadd7163c14`, in a fresh checkout with no `lychee/missing-report.md`:

```sh
LYCHEE_OUTPUT=lychee/missing-report.md LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE=2 node scripts/check-web-archive.mjs
```

Expected: nonzero status explaining that the failed checker produced no report. Current missing-file branch explicitly sets `all_archived=true` and exits/returns 0. This can suppress the workflow's final failure condition when lychee crashes, cannot write its report, or the configured paths disagree. The missing-file branch itself is the static reproduction; downloaded template reference code was inspected without executing it.

Source: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/0ece2cf2c2745c3574ffb65dbabdfcadd7163c14/scripts/check-web-archive.mjs#L313

This differs from the previously reported non-HTTP parsing and recovered-link aggregation defects: there is no report to parse at all.

## Workaround

Make the workflow fail on any nonzero lychee exit, independently of `all_archived`; use archive URLs only as repair suggestions. Preserve the report as an artifact with `if-no-files-found: error`.

## Suggested code fix

Treat a missing report as an error (throw or return 1), write `all_archived=false`, and add a subprocess regression test with a nonexistent `LYCHEE_OUTPUT` and a nonzero checker exit. The test must assert a nonzero process exit and no `all_archived=true` output. Handle an unreadable or empty/malformed report after a failed checker the same way.

The downstream PR implements a missing-report regression test and an independent final lychee exit gate. No network or Wayback access is needed to reproduce this branch.

check-file-size.rs excludes files whose absolute path merely contains target or .git (src/retarget.rs, .github/**, any checkout named *target*)
body:
## Summary

`scripts/check-file-size.rs` excludes a file when `target`, `.git` or `node_modules` occurs **anywhere in its absolute path as a substring**. Oversized sources whose names merely contain one of these words (`src/retarget.rs`, `src/target_matcher.rs`, and every Rust file under `.github/`, because `.git` is a substring of `.github`) are never measured, and in a checkout whose directory name contains one (for example a repository called `target-cli`, checked out by `actions/checkout` as `/home/runner/work/target-cli/target-cli`) **every** file is skipped and the gate reports "All files are within the line limit".

Code (template `main` at 265219d):

https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/265219d098ec1c6acbe6749562c2f3dc057f0df8/scripts/check-file-size.rs#L51-L60

```rust
let path_str = path.to_string_lossy();
EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
    .iter()
    .any(|pattern| path_str.contains(pattern))
```

`WalkDir::new(cwd)` ([L123](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/265219d098ec1c6acbe6749562c2f3dc057f0df8/scripts/check-file-size.rs#L123)) yields absolute paths, so the checkout location takes part in the match. It is also not pruned with `filter_entry`, so a real `target/` tree is still walked in full and only filtered afterwards.

## Reproduction

```bash
work=$(mktemp -d)
long() { mkdir -p "$(dirname "$1")"; yes x | head -n 1001 > "$1"; }
long "$work/rust-app/src/retarget.rs"
long "$work/rust-app/src/target_matcher.rs"
long "$work/target-cli/src/main.rs"
(cd "$work/rust-app"   && rust-script /path/to/template/scripts/check-file-size.rs); echo "exit $?"
(cd "$work/target-cli" && rust-script /path/to/template/scripts/check-file-size.rs); echo "exit $?"
```

Output (all three files have 1001 lines, the limit is 1000):

```
Checking source files for maximum 1000 lines (warning above 900) and documentation for maximum 2500 lines (warning above 2250)...

All files are within the line limit

exit 0
...
All files are within the line limit

exit 0
```

We hit this in link-foundation/link-cli (issue 134, pull request 135): `rust/src/sequences/target_matcher.rs` was never checked. The full script and its log are kept in that pull request under `dev/log/issues/134/pulls/135/scripts/template-file-size-substring-exclusion.sh` and `dev/log/issues/134/pulls/135/analysis/template-file-size-repro.txt`.

## Workaround

Do not name source files or the checkout directory with `target`, `.git` or `node_modules` in them.

## Suggested fix

Match whole path components **relative to the scanned root** and prune excluded directories while walking:

```rust
fn should_exclude(path: &Path, root: &Path) -> bool {
    let relative = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(path);
    relative.components().any(|component| {
        EXCLUDE_DIRS.iter().any(|dir| component.as_os_str() == *dir)
    })
}

for entry in WalkDir::new(&cwd)
    .into_iter()
    .filter_entry(|entry| !should_exclude(entry.path(), &cwd))
{ /* ... */ }
```

plus a regression test that creates `src/retarget.rs` and `.github/scripts/tool.rs` in a temporary root and expects both to be reported. link-cli applies exactly this in `rust/scripts/check-file-size.rs` (test `exclusions_match_whole_components_not_substrings`).

title: Adopt JavaScript-first parity gates and bulk drafting standard
body:
Adds the JavaScript-first development standard from link-assistant/router#759 while retaining existing contributor and CI guidance. The templates receive a reusable strict gate requiring source SHA verification, native tests, parity and translation checks; adoption still needs project-specific executable checks and dependencies on every existing Rust workflow. Hive Mind receives additive rules for bulk drafts, one push owner, complete failure collection, and bounded local work.

This is an adoption draft, not a claim of implemented full native parity. CI is intentionally skipped for this documentation/template proposal so existing ungated Rust workflows cannot start before the strict JavaScript stage has been integrated.

Validation: applied against immutable source `265219d098ec1c6acbe6749562c2f3dc057f0df8`; all existing documentation lines preserved; source-SHA and action pins reviewed; reusable workflow passed actionlint.

Closes #196. Related: https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/759.
